If you have Netflix, it's totally viewable right now and to be honest I kind of really want to talk about this movie but am aware that a discussion about it might generate more views and people might get upset that at my behest spent an hour or so of their lives they will never get back.

That being said some spoilers will be included, but there's no real big reveal. I'm not ruining the 6th sense for you is all I'm saying here.

That being said.

This movie queued on my netflix with a 3 and a half star rating. I am aware that the Netflix star rating is supposed to be related to how you personally have rated movies and not their general rating and usually Netflix is pretty spot on but this happened and for a moment after the movie was over I was seriously questioning my tastes in movies and how something could have gone so far south. anyway, enough preamble ramble here's the meat of the issue:

The Sisterhood of Night is advertised in the blurb as :"Three teenagers become the targets of a modern day Salem witch trial after they are accused of being part of the sinister secret network(Read: sister hood of the night)"

Anyway, basically these girls are part of their own little high school clique and are not altogether that popular, but they engage in a sort of ritualized confessional at night in weird places and therefor seem different and obscure. When word gets out of their weird secret meetings, curiosity is aroused in their local peer group and rumors circulate as to the nature and undertakings in these "secret meetings".

A rival clique's Alpha Girl has a problem with said Sisterhood (but secretly wants to be included as a member) and sneaks out one night to spy on a meeting. She is caught and told to leave.

She then proceeds to make up a serious of very serious accusations including sexual molestation and satanic undertones about the sister hood. This sparks a localized controversy as parents and teachers alike are concerned that some super nefarious shit is going down with their daughters or whatever.

This is further compounded by the fact that other girls who have no affiliation to the "Sisterhood" also "Come forward" to confess of atrocities that never happened. Creating a sort of tragic bandwagon of popularity and sympathy for abuses that never occurred. This activity becomes a minor internet sensation. (Think like... McCarthyism, but high school girls in a popularity contest, so possibly even more cruel and deviant.)

This leads to the rival alpha girl conscripting a male crush of one of the sisterhoods members to lure her out to some location under the guise of being interested in her, and then having him, her and I think members of some sports team strip her and film her with the intention of using the video for some kind of public shaming stunt. The video surfaces on the internet, the girl is socially rejected and ultimately kills herself.

No charges are brought against anyone, even though the video clearly has Rival Alpha verbally tormenting sisterhood girl while some males hold her naked body exposed to the camera.

This brings us to the final climactic end scene where:

The Leader of the Sisterhood of the night and her three closest friends start a dance routine up to the door of the Alpha Rivals house where she (The Rival) admits that "I only wanted to be a part of your group) and the leader of the sister hood then symbolicly includes her in their little dance ritual and off they all go happily dancing together. Then the leader of the sisterhood voice can be heard monologuing over this scene about how other sisterhoods are forming all over the place and yeah rah women and acceptance.

So.

I am led to believe that the implication of the ending that the following is acceptable behaivour:

1: one can in fact issue a series of incredibly destructive false accusations that could land the accused in prison for large amounts of time and that is acceptable, even encouraged as a means of social interactivity.

2: One can video tape the verbal and physical torture and humiliation of a person with no social or legal consequences, even if said torture and humiliation lead to the suicide of the victim.

3: After engaging in such malicious and selfish behaviors one is to be accepted into a peer group with little or no social or legal consequences.

What the ever loving fuck.

I could see the strong christian undertones of forgiveness and acceptance, but the fact remains that this person lied about you in a fashion that could render prison. Not jail, PRISON time. This person humiliated and tortured a friend of yours, leading to that friends suicide. This person effectively turned a whole community against 4 girls under the premise of sexual abuse and drug use and then invited others to perpetuate the lie and include lies of their own, even to the point of using a love interest to lure one of said girls to a private location for actual torture and humiliation, and that is all perfectly socially acceptable.

I mean. Am I missing something? Can someone explain a meaning or subtext I'm missing here?

The ONLY other subtext I can gather would be:

Small unpopular fringe groups who have been violated by the popular majority groups should accept this hazing as a blessing and befriend those who would humiliate and torture others like them because.... Jesus? And those in the majority groups can engage in this hateful behavior with little or no consequence what so ever because... Jesus?

I just don't get it.

Maybe one of you can better elaborate what I'm missing in this movie, because I just cannot see how this is considered a "Good Young woman/girly coming of age movie."
